coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Saturday long run: 12–14 miles, rolling terrain, Z2 effort (130–145 bpm). You're 20 days out and in taper; this is your last meaningful volume injection before you strip back further next week. Your resting HR jumped to 74 (vs. 30-day avg of 66.5) and recovery score sits at 46/100—both yellow flags that you're still fatigued from the peak phase. Keep this run steady and controlled; do NOT chase pace or vert. The Julian Alps will demand sustained aerobic power on technical ground, not speed. Treat this as a dress rehearsal for race-day fueling and pacing discipline.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Consume 60–80g of carbs per hour during the run (sports drink, gels, or real food if your stomach tolerates it on longer efforts). Your 70% sleep efficiency suggests incomplete recovery; don't leave fuel on the table. Post-run, hit a 3:1 or 4:1 carb-to-protein ratio within 30 minutes—aim for 50g carbs + 15g protein (banana + Greek yogurt, or rice cakes + almond butter). You've logged 27.6 miles this week already; your glycogen stores are drawn down heading into the final push toward race day.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your 8.3-hour night had only 70% efficiency—you're sleeping long but not sleeping well. Before bed tonight, skip caffeine after 2 PM, keep the room cool (65–68°F), and avoid screens 30 minutes before sleep. Elevated resting HR and moderate recovery score mean your sympathetic nervous system is still activated; prioritize parasympathetic reset. Consider 5–10 minutes of easy breathing work or yin yoga post-run. Aim for 8+ hours tonight with the goal of pushing that efficiency above 80%—you need genuine recovery, not just time in bed.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the psychological sweet spot of taper—fit, sharp, but naturally restless. Today's long run is your final confidence builder; use it to refine your race nutrition strategy, test your gear setup, and mentally rehearse the high-altitude technical sections around Kranjska Gora. Trust the training: 20 days is enough time to arrive fresh if you execute next week's volume cuts without panic. The urge to squeeze in extra work is normal and wrong; your edge comes from showing up rested, not from one more hard session.
